criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use an elevated oblique city-map view with visible structure sides.
Both frame the playable network across most of the viewport.
different: REFERENCE is closer and more terrain-relief-driven; CANDIDATE is broader and shallower.
Ground axes and landmark framing differ materially, with more isolated upright sprites in CANDIDATE.

evidence.observation: Close oblique framing emphasizes ravines, large plants, and a dense city edge.
Wider, flatter overview exposes longer routes and more separated interactive structures.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both maps combine dense housing, roads, pylons, and industrial districts.
Both concentrate urban mass toward the right and industrial mass toward the left.
different: REFERENCE has stronger foreground massing and large industrial anchors.
CANDIDATE leaves broader open corridors between active assets despite a dense background.

evidence.observation: Residential blocks densely fill the right half around the selected substation.
Two large industrial complexes strongly occupy the left side.
Background buildings are numerous, but active facilities remain widely separated by open road and terrain areas.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both show a dark winding channel cutting through dry brown terrain.
Both channels have rocky banks and network crossings nearby.
different: REFERENCE presents a deeper, darker ravine-like channel; CANDIDATE water is flatter and more uniformly brown.
CANDIDATE has two conspicuous attached bridges, while REFERENCE crossings are dominated by pylons and conductors.

evidence.observation: A sinuous recessed channel runs from the central map toward the lower-left edge.
A shallower winding channel is crossed by two large illuminated bridges.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Plants remain the largest silhouettes and pylons remain smaller repeated units.
Substations and civic facilities occupy an intermediate visual tier in both.
different: REFERENCE uses larger plant masses as dominant regional landmarks.
CANDIDATE foreground buildings and facilities approach pylon or transformer scale more unevenly.

evidence.observation: The upper-left generating plant is substantially larger than nearby towers and houses.
A second broad industrial complex anchors the lower-left region.
Large isolated building sprites, small substations, and pylons share a less graduated scale range.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use blackened riveted metal, brown soil and concrete, amber windows, and cyan accents.
Both maintain a cohesive weathered industrial finish across map and overlays.
different: REFERENCE has richer cracked-ground relief and stronger metallic highlights.
CANDIDATE midtones are more uniformly sepia and several map sprites appear flatter or greyer.

evidence.observation: Detailed cracked soil, dark masonry, metal machinery, and amber pin lighting remain distinct.
The same brown-black-amber material family is present with a flatter overall wash.
Riveted black-metal framing closely matches the map's industrial material language.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use cyan routes linking pylons, substations, and facilities.
Both distinguish a troubled or planned segment with a warm contrasting color.
different: REFERENCE conductors glow strongly and read as direct tower-to-tower energy paths.
CANDIDATE routes are thinner schematic double lines, with overlaps and less precise visible attachment.

evidence.observation: Bright cyan conductors and node glows clearly trace the energized path through successive towers.
A short amber-orange segment visibly identifies the stressed connection.
Thin cyan polylines cover the map, while the lower-right route changes to a dashed pink-red segment.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use a riveted chrome top bar, a left vertical build kit, and a right inspector.
Panel proportions and edge placement leave a similarly large integrated map area.
different: CANDIDATE uses denser, smaller text in the inspector and top status blocks.
REFERENCE gives the selected object portrait and capacity state stronger visual prominence.

evidence.observation: Segmented black-metal status modules span the top edge.
A closely matched segmented riveted status bar spans the same edge.
Large portrait, capacity line, unavailable state, and condition form a clear inspector hierarchy.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both visibly identify a +8°C heat event.
Both apply an amber-brown atmosphere, bright sun, and drought-like terrain to the same grid-world type.
different: REFERENCE has stronger sun bloom and more explicit cracked, scorched ground.
CANDIDATE relies more on a uniform brown tint and status text for the heat read.

evidence.observation: The top status visibly reads HEAT +8°C.
A bright low sun and intense amber haze dominate the upper-right world.
The top event module visibly includes 폭염 +8°C.

criteria.label: PARITY
similar: Both use a centered four-cell bottom strip with black riveted chrome.
Both have nearly identical normalized footprint and an active second cell outlined in cyan.
CANDIDATE visibly includes progress, current event, result, and next-stage states.
different: CANDIDATE uses denser stage text and small status markers, a minor hierarchy variation.

evidence.observation: Four evenly sized bottom controls sit in a compact integrated metal tray with the second highlighted.
Four event-stage cells occupy the same centered footprint, with construction progress, an active event, result, and next labels.
